item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) The Reaction God
item.content:encoded:
This is one of those SCP ideas where the title sounds more interesting than the actual idea.

From the title, I figured that this was maybe a riff on the "highly engaging" "genre" of "reaction videos" like the Fine Brothers do, and this would somehow be a deity formed of the mass's gormless consumption of them. Instead, it's… kind of confusing. A being that gathers people up into a theater and exposes them to information that they're not meant to know? It doesn't really tie into the 'reaction' of the title, and the description is kind of muddy on top of that. I don't really get what kind of narrative you're going for here.

No Greenlight.

item.title: Seeking Greenlights: A Second Reflection (accounting for criticisms))
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid creature with smooth black skin and no features except for its mouth. You can only see its reflection, although it does not work when the reflection is recorded. As such, an image cannot be provided unless it is an illustration of the specimen.
It can phase through everything that isn't living flesh (e.g. LIVING animals, LIVING humans), but this ability is nullified if its temperature is lowered below -50 degrees Celsius, or 223 degrees Kelvin.
Once in containment, SCP-XXXX does not require any sort of furniture in its containment cell (made of mirror-like reflective metal to ensure its presence), only needing a cooling system to keep it from phasing out of the room. It does need to be fed, and its meals consist of wild animals and, if a test takes an unfortunate turn, an unlucky Class-D personnel.
It acts like an aggressive and predatory animal despite its humanoid form, and will attack anything, including other SCPs. It will claw at the walls of its cell, and if it breaks the cooling system, it can breach containment. This aggression is seemingly nullified while SCP-XXXX is in the presence of SCP-XXXX-B.
SCP-XXXX-B is the infant born from SCP-XXXX. It resembles a humanoid infant with lighter colored skin than its parent. It shares the same invisibility as its parent, but has not yet displayed any signs of aggression.
Central Narrative: The details of SCP-XXXX's containment are yet undisclosed, but many researchers in the Foundation have suggested that it be reclassified to Thaumiel due to its aforementioned aggression. While the subject is still up for debate, its classification remains Keter, due to its extreme aggression and repeated attempts at breaching containment.
At some point, some people suggested that SCP-XXXX could be the last piece in the puzzle that is the destruction of SCP-682, but due to the incredibly high likelihood of failure, the possibility has been dropped completely.
In the months following the containment of SCP-XXXX, it is discovered to have been pregnant, and it gives birth to SCP-XXXX-B while in containment. This, followed by repeated sightings of SCP-XXXX out in the wild despite it being in containment confirms that SCP-XXXX is not an isolated anomaly, but an entire species of creatures with the same abilities.

item.title: A skull that loves to sing Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: A skull that is sapient that can make sound anywhere in the world as well as hear everything that is being done in the world. The skull can also make exact imitations of sound and voices. The skull also knows languages that were wiped out and some that aren't even recorded in history. The skull can move its lower jaw but doesn't need it to make sound. The pitch of the sound made from the skull seems to be limitless.

Central Narrative: The skull was obtained from a cult that was taking skulls from people. It was sent when a police officer that was actually a foundation personnel was asked by the skull for help. On the way to a site the skull conducted a interview with a researcher at the site. Through the interviews it is revealed that the it became this because it saw something it shouldn't. The skull suffers a tremendous amount of mental damage as it can hear all of the suffering of the world. Singing in cafeteria however has been an emotional anchor an idea thought by the foundation to relieve it of some pain. This has worked even though only a little. The skull is going through therapy every week.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The hook is show readers a fairly simple idea but the more you read into the story you realise the skull has a very mysterious and sad past through the interviews conducted during therapy sessions.

Additional Notes: This was inspired by SCP-774 as a skull that made sound. I then added hear no evil, speak no evil, see no evil concept and worked the skull's backstory around that. This my first time writing an scp so any feedback is appreciated. Also if anything isn't clear please let me know

item.title: In an alternate universe. Foundations similar to SCP and GOC have a war
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: A person with no record of existing claiming to be part of the 05 council seemingly teleports to a site. They warn us about a dangerous war happening 5 years in the future between the CID (Capture, Imprison, Defend) and the WWAC (WorldWide anomaly coalition) It turns out. The person warning us accidentally went to a parallel universe at the same time instead of time traveling 5 years before in their universe. The person is questioned and we learn about how the war started and what happened. Then we try to figure out how to send them back to their universe 5 years in the past.

Central Narrative: In the parallel universe, The CID finds an anomaly with reality-altering abilities and kill half of the 05 Council. The WWAC accidentally made the anomaly by trying to kill a different one. The CID learn about this and they try to start a war with them. Overruled by the ethics committee, they try to keep things peaceful. One 05 council member goes rogue and sends SCP-662 to eliminate the heads of the GOC. That's all I have so far but if this gets greenlighted, I will write the entire thing.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP article takes place as a story (similar to SCP-5000) and the SCP foundation tries to get into contact with the GOC to tell them what happened and to avoid it.

Additional Notes: I'm not that of an experienced writer and I may need help with this one.

item.title: Re: Insights of insanity
item.content:encoded:
My main issue here is I'm not getting a sense for any sort of conflict or stakes involved with the disclosure of this information. In essence you are implying to the reader that this dreamer entity exists and all else (obfuscated by a level of mud and crosslinks that frankly sounds like it'd be annoying to dig through), but without something to draw readers in I don't think it'll hit particularly hard.

In addition I'm rather confused about how this cult came into this information. How did they get access to the eyes?

Additionally you seem like you're importing the themes of knowledge coming at a cost from Bloodborne but without a real effort to reconcile with those themes. Bloodborne already did the thing where acquiring knowledge makes you mad — using that mechanic as shorthand here just feels uninteresting and disconnected.

item.title: Re: Seeking greenlights (Re-do due to breaking word limit)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Emotional/ exploration

Elevator Pitch: What happens when you put a space in between the past, and the present? This is a liminal space. What happens when you put someone in a dimension of nothing but liminal spaces? Would that affect someone? What if they could spread if they weren't monitored?

Central Narrative:The narrative of this SCP to show liminal spaces activate memories and experiences we have never had, SCP-XXXX is a rotting wooden door attached to a concrete structure that has been ripped out of its original place, the inside being bigger than it's exterior. The inside contains a series of endless hallways with wooden doors lining each wall that lead deeper into SCP-XXXX with entryways to the next hallway every 10 miles. Each door that has never been unopened before leads to a completely random room correlating to the subject's suppressed memories, intentions, and or emotions, often being broken in ways like repeating sections or missing areas entirely, or random items in said rooms. The door must always stay closed for it is opened and consistently stayed open for longer than 20 minutes, the warped reality will spread to everything, including organic matter, concrete is found to be the least affected by this property. Exposure longer than 4 hours leads to a steady loss of direction.
So, what happens when someone is put inside for long periods of time? This is about a D class being put into SCP-XXXX for longer than a week. This leads the D class to remember who he is, his real name, and just why he was put on death row and forced to be a test subject in the foundation. This leads to acceptance of his actions, knowing that the foundation will mostly cut him off for retaining this info, he must come to terms knowing that he will either never make it out of here, or be killed by the foundation.

show block
hide block

hook/Attention-Grabber: These spaces have popped up on the internet all over, oftentimes people saying it feels oddly familiar with an overwhelming sense of deja vu. This SCP takes this idea of Liminal Spaces and turns it into an endless expanse of repeating rooms and endless mazes of warped reality, turning it into an eerie dimension of exploration.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP, spare me no slack.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello hello The Grinning Man! Welcome to the Wiki! I'm Ralliston, a site author and a member of the Community Outreach Team - with this helpful little comment, I'll try to help you find your way around the site and link a bunch of useful places and links that will help you in your SCP journey. I would say that your interest in the Foundation through its weird ideas and pictures is not really all that surprising - here, it's all about the weird and supernatural, isn't it? An insane imagination is a pretty good thing here, since you know what they say - the weirder the better :P

Without further ado though, let's click the collapsible, shall we? :)

+ show block
– hide block

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our Sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts, which are in-works articles. Using it, you can link the drafts to reviewers to get their opinions on them before posting. It really helps everyone out a lot.

For brainstorming concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by experienced members of the community if you need help refining and fleshing out your concept. Have to downvote due to totally inadequate descriptions of military operations, making me unable to suspend my disbelief. There is very little hope for any other nation to launch any sort of amphibious invasion of American soil without liberal use of nuclear weapons. That the war lasted for so long implies a strangely half-hearted deployment of strategic nuclear weapons - when the deliberate launching of one would inevitably set off a counter-strike of greater magnitude. Mutually assured destruction.

The war never happened because the war as it's described in the document is too silly to have existed. Kauai can only be taken if all US air and naval presence from Hawaii and surrounding regions have been destroyed. This implies the annihilation of the US Pacific Fleet. Even if our 2020's China were mobilized for war, they still have no experience nor even doctrine for conducting naval operations of that scale. China's military today isn't even geared towards Pacific dominance. Its main concern is projecting regional power towards Taiwan and India. Its naval stance is strikingly defensive. Our PRC has the largest coastal defense force in the world, bristling with battery upon battery of anti-ship missiles. It is defensive because it doesn't have the political and financial resources to be offensive. Because it is the weaker military. A poorer 2000's China simply cannot hope to do anything about Hawaii, much less the US mainland.

The only real offensive capabilities China has against the US would be its strategic nuclear arsenal. It is tiny when compared to its American counterpart. The moment China uses one on the United States, to attack a military installation, then the Americans will use a liberal definition of the term 'military installation' and launch a significantly more devastating counter-attack. If the PRC decides to strike at a population center, then the US is sure to nuke Beijing, Shanghai, Nanking and everything else.

A total war with nukes lasting this long between two combatant nations of vastly differing capabilities is simply not possible. Your military science is unsound.

item.title: Re: The Mother of Meteorites
item.content:encoded:
I rather like this idea, think it's a keeper.

+ Planetary Intergalactic
- Intergalactic Planetary

Do I need to make them more dangerous?

No. I do think there should be some reference to the inherent danger and containment challenge they pose, but you nailed the appeal in your hook description: These are a great example of an anomaly where conservationist!Foundation kicks in, and you see Protect working on both sides of the masquerade for some whimsical oddity.

Class and containment-wise, they're a low-threat Keter, maybe even the esoteric class Cernunnos if you're feeling daring- They're fairly harmless as long as they don't land on anything/anyone or blow open the masquerade, but they can't be properly contained without disrupting their life cycle, and the Foundation doesn't like driving things extinct. I'd suggest having containment take the form of the Foundation working to steer them away from populated areas, maybe even to non-Earth nesting grounds. (It's been long established that the Foundation has a manned moon base, if they need Earth-like conditions to incubate.)

On the biology front, silicon-based life is vaguely plausible. Hard science-wise there's some issues with solvency and stability, but life has solved harder problems. If you have them be silicone-based (silicon-carbon mix), not only does the plausibility skyrocket, you start dealing with the sort of hyperdurable materials actual spacecraft are made out of. If you wanted them to be from Earth originally, you could hint at them being large multicellular relatives of corals or stromatolites (microrganisms that essentially 3D-print rock formations, may be some of the earliest Earth-life) You might also take notes from deep sea life on the breeding logistics; strategies include parasitic mating so a partner is always available, seasonal breeding swarms in otherwise solitary species, and opportunistic mating with sperm or fertilized eggs kept in stasis until conditions are right.

Story-wise I think you've got a good framework for the narrative thought out, though I'd suggest looking for a strong twist or emotional arc to tie it all together. It doesn't have to be a "and now we're all doomed" twist or Shakespearean tragedy, mind you- just something that your reader can get emotionally invested in (say, the Foundation's struggles to get them to breed in that moon base end in a first successful clutch launching into space), or something that surprises the reader and has us seeing these things in a different way at the end.

That said, think I'm a Greenlight

item.title: SCP Idea: An Age-Old Industry
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation finds hundreds of dead whales in the middle of the woods, with no idea how they got there. Turns out to be foul play.

Central Narrative: On an otherwise idyllic day in a sleepy small town in British Columbia, a 60-ton Right Whale materializes on top of someone's house and makes a big mess. The Foundation swoops in and covers the whole thing up. Not a big deal. Shit like this happens every day in the Foundation-verse.

Then some hikers find the remains of another whale impaled on a tree. Now the Foundation's is interested. They establish a task force to look for more dead whales in the Canadian back-country, and end up finding (literal) tons of them in various stages of decomposition. Dead whales in the treetops. Dead whales 300 kilometers inland. Dead whales embedded in the ground, or dashed out on rocks, or totally pureed as if they've been dropped from a great height. They do some cursory biological / genetic analysis on the remains. Turns out that they all come from a specific part of the Bering Sea.

Through means that I have yet to think up, the Foundation learns that the whales were teleported into the woods by poachers with anomalous hunting technology. Their intent was to beam the poor animals to a "chop shop" in the States, where they could be dissected and sold for oil and ambergris. Because their teleporters were faulty over long distances, only about 30% of the whales made it to the chop shop. The rest were randomly dispersed in the space between. When the poachers were confronted by a police patrol boat, they tried to teleport themselves the hell out of Dodge and met the same grisly fate as the other 70%.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a narrative mystery, with enough inherent wackiness to make it compelling.

item.title: (Seeking Greenlight) The Reaction God
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes!

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy/Serious

Elevator Pitch: A non-corporeal entity takes random individuals' appearance throughout the places it came across. The entity existed in an unknown multi-dimensional location.

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is a non-corporeal entity that takes random individuals' appearance throughout the places it came across. The entity shows no signs of hostility, is capable of speech, and understands all sorts of languages. SCP-XXXX would usually gather random individuals from a universe, or different universes that are chosen by it into a massive cinematic room created by itself and would expose to those individuals all information that it wants them to know or the information that they must/want to know/learn, regardless of whether if the information that the entity exposed could lead to big consequences.

SCP-XXXX was first discovered when it was in the middle of gathering a group of peoples into its cinematic/theatre room; this time, it takes an adult form. One of the individuals it has gathered is the Foundation's researcher on his way to work. As the researcher has stayed undercover for a long period and witnessed the entity exposed the information of the Foundation to all gathered individuals.

The researcher has reported back to the Foundation from what he has seen, including each gathered individuals' reaction. This has soon resulted in the dispatching of MTF Lambda-5; however, where he is being held with the other individuals is unknown. Because the Foundation's satellite couldn't locate where it is, they've had no choice but to aboard the mission.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The idea of having an entity that came across the multiverse and did not expose its true form and attempts to spill out information that're strictly forbidden not to be revealed under any circumstances.

Additional Notes: This is just a summary of the SCP; due to exceeding 400 words, I must shorten it. If you want the full, then ask me for a draft.
